title: Hub prose: Government Spending & the Budget, Explained

sources.label: House Rule XXI — Restrictions on Certain Bills (119th Congress)

claims.claim: The federal fiscal year begins on October 1.
claims.sourceSpan: the fiscal year beginning on October 1 of such year

claims.claim: Under 2 U.S.C. 632(a), the Congress "shall complete action on a concurrent resolution on the budget."
claims.sourceSpan: shall complete action on a concurrent resolution on the budget

claims.claim: The deadline for the budget resolution is on or before April 15 of each year.
claims.sourceSpan: On or before April 15 of each year

claims.claim: The resolution is for "the fiscal year beginning on October 1 of such year."
claims.sourceSpan: the fiscal year beginning on October 1 of such year

claims.claim: The resolution sets appropriate levels for "at least each of the 4 ensuing fiscal years."
claims.sourceSpan: at least each of the 4 ensuing fiscal years

claims.claim: The concurrent resolution covers "totals of new budget authority and outlays."
claims.sourceSpan: totals of new budget authority and outlays

claims.claim: The concurrent resolution covers "total Federal revenues."
claims.sourceSpan: total Federal revenues

claims.claim: The concurrent resolution covers "the surplus or deficit in the budget."
claims.sourceSpan: the surplus or deficit in the budget

claims.claim: Under House Rule XXI, clause 2(a)(1), an appropriation "may not be reported in a general appropriation bill, and may not be in order as an amendment thereto, for an expenditure not previously authorized by law."
claims.sourceSpan: may not be reported in a general appropriation bill, and may not be in order as an amendment thereto, for an expenditure not previously authorized by law

claims.claim: Rule XXI, clause 2(a)(1) makes an exception "to continue appropriations for public works and objects that are already in progress."
claims.sourceSpan: except to continue appropriations for public works and objects that are already in progress

claims.claim: Parliamentary annotations of House Rule XXI record that "a joint resolution only containing continuing appropriations for diverse agencies to provide funds until regular appropriation bills are enacted" has been held not to be a general appropriation bill for purposes of the rule.
claims.sourceSpan: a joint resolution only containing continuing appropriations for diverse agencies to provide funds until regular appropriation bills are enacted

claims.claim: The precedent for CR status appears as Sec. 1044 in the annotations to House Rule XXI.
Under 31 U.S.C. 1341, an officer or employee may not "make or authorize an expenditure or obligation exceeding an amount available in an appropriation or fund for the expenditure or obligation."
claims.sourceSpan: make or authorize an expenditure or obligation exceeding an amount available in an appropriation or fund for the expenditure or obligation

claims.claim: 1341 further bars an officer or employee to "involve either government in a contract or obligation for the payment of money before an appropriation is made unless authorized by law."
claims.sourceSpan: involve either government in a contract or obligation for the payment of money before an appropriation is made unless authorized by law

claims.claim: 31 U.S.C. 1342 provides that an officer or employee "may not accept voluntary services for either government or employ personal services exceeding that authorized by law except for emergencies involving the safety of human life or the protection of property."
claims.sourceSpan: may not accept voluntary services for either government or employ personal services exceeding that authorized by law except for emergencies involving the safety of human life or the protection of property

claims.claim: The 1342 emergency exception "does not include ongoing, regular functions of government the suspension of which would not imminently threaten the safety of human life or the protection of property."
claims.sourceSpan: does not include ongoing, regular functions of government the suspension of which would not imminently threaten the safety of human life or the protection of property

claims.claim: 31 U.S.C. 1341(c)(2) requires that each furloughed employee "shall be paid for the period of the lapse in appropriations."
claims.sourceSpan: shall be paid for the period of the lapse in appropriations

claims.claim: Each excepted employee required to perform work "shall be paid for such work."
claims.sourceSpan: shall be paid for such work

claims.claim: Payment is "at the employee's standard rate of pay."
claims.sourceSpan: at the employee's standard rate of pay

claims.claim: Payment is required "at the earliest date possible after the lapse in appropriations ends."
claims.sourceSpan: at the earliest date possible after the lapse in appropriations ends

claims.claim: Under 2 U.S.C. 641(a), a concurrent resolution on the budget can specify totals for new budget authority.
claims.sourceSpan: (A) new budget authority for such fiscal year

claims.claim: 641(a) covers revenues.
claims.sourceSpan: specify the total amount by which revenues are to be changed

claims.claim: 641(a) covers "the statutory limit on the public debt."
claims.sourceSpan: the statutory limit on the public debt

claims.claim: Reconciliation directs "committees having jurisdiction."
claims.sourceSpan: committees having jurisdiction

claims.claim: The direction is to "determine and recommend changes."
claims.sourceSpan: determine and recommend changes

claims.claim: Senate debate on any reconciliation bill "shall be limited to not more than 20 hours" (2 U.S.C. 641(e)(2)).
claims.sourceSpan: shall be limited to not more than 20 hours

claims.claim: Under 2 U.S.C. 644, a point of order lies against "material extraneous to the instructions to a committee."
claims.sourceSpan: material extraneous to the instructions to a committee

claims.claim: The point of order can be "sustained by the Chair."
claims.sourceSpan: sustained by the Chair

claims.claim: If sustained, the offending part "shall be deemed stricken from the bill and may not be offered as an amendment from the floor."
claims.sourceSpan: shall be deemed stricken from the bill and may not be offered as an amendment from the floor

claims.claim: 644(b)(1) includes a provision that "produces changes in outlays or revenues which are merely incidental to the non-budgetary components of the provision."
claims.sourceSpan: produces changes in outlays or revenues which are merely incidental to the non-budgetary components of the provision

claims.claim: 644(b)(1) further includes a provision that increases net outlays or decreases revenues after the covered fiscal years, subject to the netting qualifier "and such increases or decreases are greater than outlay reductions or revenue increases resulting from other provisions in such title in such year."
claims.sourceSpan: and such increases or decreases are greater than outlay reductions or revenue increases resulting from other provisions in such title in such year

claims.claim: Under 2 U.S.C. 601 there is "an office of the Congress to be known as the Congressional Budget Office."
claims.sourceSpan: an office of the Congress to be known as the Congressional Budget Office

claims.claim: The Director is "appointed by the Speaker of the House of Representatives and the President pro tempore of the Senate after considering recommendations received from the Committees on the Budget of the House and the Senate, without regard to political affiliation and solely on the basis of his fitness to perform his duties."
claims.sourceSpan: appointed by the Speaker of the House of Representatives and the President pro tempore of the Senate after considering recommendations received from the Committees on the Budget of the House and the Senate, without regard to political affiliation and solely on the basis of his fitness to perform his duties

claims.claim: "The term of office of the Director shall be 4 years."
claims.sourceSpan: The term of office of the Director shall be 4 years

claims.claim: Under 2 U.S.C. 601(d), the Director is authorized "to secure information, data, estimates, and statistics directly from the various departments, agencies, and establishments of the executive branch of Government and the regulatory agencies and commissions of the Government."
claims.sourceSpan: to secure information, data, estimates, and statistics directly from the various departments, agencies, and establishments of the executive branch of Government and the regulatory agencies and commissions of the Government

claims.claim: Those departments and agencies "shall furnish the Director any available material which he determines to be necessary."
claims.sourceSpan: shall furnish the Director any available material which he determines to be necessary

claims.claim: Under 2 U.S.C. 601(f): "For the purposes of revenue legislation which is income, estate and gift, excise, and payroll taxes (i.e., Social Security)."
claims.sourceSpan: For the purposes of revenue legislation which is income, estate and gift, excise, and payroll taxes (i.e., Social Security)

claims.claim: For those revenue-legislation purposes, the Congressional Budget Office "shall use exclusively during that session of Congress revenue estimates provided to it by the Joint Committee on Taxation."
claims.sourceSpan: shall use exclusively during that session of Congress revenue estimates provided to it by the Joint Committee on Taxation

claims.claim: 601(f)'s scope qualifier is that the revenue legislation must be "considered or enacted in any session of Congress."
claims.sourceSpan: considered or enacted in any session of Congress

claims.claim: Earlier draft labeled 2 U.S.C. 644 as "the Byrd rule."
claims.sourceSpan: Extraneous provisions
claims.verify: The token "Byrd" appears in none of the seven registered source files (grep across ref-text/ returned zero matches). The section is titled "Extraneous provisions" and the enclosing division is "Extraneous matter in reconciliation legislation." The "Byrd rule" label is a common-usage name never used by the statute itself and cannot be sourced from the registered evidence. Fixed by rewriting "The Byrd rule, at 2 U.S.C. 644, lets any Senator raise a point of order..." to "Under 2 U.S.C. 644, on a point of order by any Senator against 'material extraneous to the instructions to a committee'..."

claims.claim: Earlier draft characterized the Senate reconciliation debate cap as "fixed 20 hours."
claims.sourceSpan: shall be limited to not more than 20 hours
claims.verify: 641(e)(2) sets a ceiling ("not more than 20 hours"), not a fixed value. Debate can end sooner. "Fixed 20 hours" inverts the direction (ceiling to floor / to a fixed quantum). Fixed by quoting the ceiling verbatim.

claims.claim: Earlier draft called CBO "nonpartisan."
claims.sourceSpan: without regard to political affiliation and solely on the basis of his fitness to perform his duties
claims.verify: Source's own descriptor of the appointment standard is "without regard to political affiliation and solely on the basis of his fitness to perform his duties" — which the draft now quotes verbatim. "Nonpartisan" is an editorial gloss that never appears in the source. Removed.

claims.claim: Earlier draft asserted CBO "produces most cost estimates" for Congress.
claims.sourceSpan: shall use exclusively during that session of Congress revenue estimates provided to it by the Joint Committee on Taxation
claims.verify: Registered source does not describe a market-share fact about who produces most cost estimates. The only volume comparison the source implies is the reverse: the tax carve-out reserves revenue estimates for the Joint Committee on Taxation. Deleted.

claims.claim: Earlier draft's paraphrase of 644(b)(1)(E) omitted the netting qualifier.
claims.sourceSpan: and such increases or decreases are greater than outlay reductions or revenue increases resulting from other provisions in such title in such year
claims.verify: Without the netting qualifier, the (E) description asserts a stricter rule than the statute imposes: (E) only triggers if the out-year increase EXCEEDS other offsetting reductions in the same title in the same year. Quote added verbatim.

claims.claim: Earlier draft quoted 601(f) as "for the purposes..." (lowercase f).
claims.sourceSpan: For the purposes of revenue legislation which is income, estate and gift, excise, and payroll taxes (i.e., Social Security)
claims.verify: Source begins subsection (f) with capital "For". Draft now matches source case.

claims.claim: Earlier draft's 1341 quote "may not make or authorize an expenditure..." was non-contiguous with source (source reads "may not— (A) make or authorize...").
claims.sourceSpan: make or authorize an expenditure or obligation exceeding an amount available in an appropriation or fund for the expenditure or obligation
claims.verify: Rewrote sentence to place "may not" outside the quotation marks so the quoted span is truly contiguous verbatim source text.

claims.claim: Earlier draft framed 601(f) with the editorial phrase "The tax carve-out is at 2 U.S.C. 601(f)."
claims.sourceSpan: For the purposes of revenue legislation which is income, estate and gift, excise, and payroll taxes (i.e., Social Security)
claims.verify: "Tax carve-out" is characterization; the source is a subsection directing use of JCT revenue estimates. Rewrote to "Under 2 U.S.C. 601(f):" — plain citation.

claims.claim: Earlier draft's H2-2 second sentence pivoted from CR precedent to the April 15 budget-resolution deadline, drifting off the section question.
claims.sourceSpan: a joint resolution only containing continuing appropriations for diverse agencies to provide funds until regular appropriation bills are enacted
claims.verify: The budget-resolution deadline is not a fact about CRs; the two are distinct instruments. Second sentence cut. Section now answers its own question from source-anchored precedent (Sec. 1044).

claims.claim: Earlier draft paraphrased 641(a) as "direct named committees to recommend changes to law to hit specified totals."
claims.sourceSpan: committees having jurisdiction
claims.verify: Source language is "committees having jurisdiction" — not "named committees." Draft rewritten to mirror source's jurisdictional standard; "hit specified totals" (colloquial gloss) replaced with source-anchored "determine and recommend changes to accomplish those totals."

claims.claim: Earlier draft asserted 644(b)(1) "has six categories."
claims.sourceSpan: Extraneous provisions
claims.verify: The count of six (A–F) is a derivation, not a single verbatim span. Under strict article-lane rules, every claim must bind to a verbatim source span. Removed the count; rewrote as "The definition at 644(b)(1) includes..." — the two illustrative provisions are quoted verbatim, no aggregate claim about the enumeration is asserted.

claims.claim: Earlier draft's tail nav paragraph read "how the Senate side complicates matters."
claims.sourceSpan: shall be limited to not more than 20 hours
claims.verify: "Complicates matters" is editorial framing. Rewrote to "how the Senate handles debate" — neutral, structural.

claims.claim: Pass-1 draft quoted "the term of office of the Director shall be 4 years" (lowercase "the"); source begins subsection (a)(3) with capital "The".
claims.sourceSpan: The term of office of the Director shall be 4 years
claims.verify: Source (a)(3): "The term of office of the Director shall be 4 years and shall expire on January 3 of the year preceding each Presidential election." The quoted fragment sits mid-sentence in the draft, silently lowercasing the source's capital "T" — the same case-mismatch class Pass 1 caught on 601(f). Fix: split the sentence at the previous quote's close so the second quote begins a new sentence introduced by "At 601(a)(3)," — the capital "T" now matches source. No editorial claim added; the 4-year term is unchanged.

claims.claim: Pass-1/Pass-2 draft split 601(f) into two quoted spans joined by the bridge word "CBO", silently dropping the source's scope qualifier "considered or enacted in any session of Congress" from between them.
claims.sourceSpan: For the purposes of revenue legislation which is income, estate and gift, excise, and payroll taxes (i.e., Social Security), considered or enacted in any session of Congress, the Congressional Budget Office shall use exclusively during that session of Congress revenue estimates provided to it by the Joint Committee on Taxation
claims.verify: Source 601(f) opens with a single continuous sentence: "For the purposes of revenue legislation which is income, estate and gift, excise, and payroll taxes (i.e., Social Security), considered or enacted in any session of Congress, the Congressional Budget Office shall use exclusively during that session of Congress revenue estimates provided to it by the Joint Committee on Taxation." The Pass-2 draft cut this into two quoted fragments joined by the bridge word "CBO", silently substituting for the source's ", considered or enacted in any session of Congress, the Congressional Budget Office ". The dropped material "considered or enacted in any session of Congress" is a substantive scope qualifier that tells the reader the JCT-only rule applies to legislation actively being considered or enacted in the session — a limitation the reader loses when the bridge word replaces it. Same class as Pass 1's 1341 split-quote fix ("may not" outside the quote marks) and the elision prohibition in ARTICLE-SPEC §7 ("A span in quotes must appear exactly in a stored source") plus README's article-lane rule ("Elision is not tolerated on articles"). Fixed by merging into one continuous verbatim quote — the full 601(f) opening sentence now appears as a single quotation from source, no elision. The two prior SUPPORTED rows for the split fragments still hold (each fragment is a verbatim substring of the merged quote), and a new SUPPORTED row was added for the previously-dropped scope qualifier.
